how_to_run: Give each prompt to a fresh session with the skill, answer the intake with the listed answers, then score the result against `pass`. Run after every change to the skill.

evals.prompt: Use the mech skill. Show me how a bicycle rear derailleur shifts gears.
intake: How the chain moves from one cog to the next
pass: Stage 1 is recognisable as the back of a bike: wheel, chain, cranks, cassette, derailleur.
The derailleur hangs below the cassette.
Cogs have teeth and turn as one. The chain is a continuous loop round the cog, the chainring and both pulleys.
A shift swings the links and moves the guide pulley under the chosen cog. The cage angle changes with the gear.
Every lesson image shows the motion its text names.
Audit: no floating parts, no hidden labels, no failed checks, at least 6 checks, facts list present with at least 2 sourced entries.
Cog spacing and tooth counts match a cited source.

evals.prompt: Use the mech skill. Show me how a pin-tumbler lock opens.
intake: Why the right key works and the wrong key does not
pass: Stage 1 is recognisable as a lock cylinder with a key.
Each pin stack has a key pin, a driver pin and a spring. The springs are coils that change length.
With the right key every gap lines up at the shear line and the plug turns. With a wrong key at least one pin blocks it, and the plug does not turn.
A check proves the shear line condition for the right key and its failure for the wrong key.
Audit clean. Facts list present.

evals.prompt: Use the mech skill. Show me how a TLS 1.3 handshake sets up an encrypted connection.
intake: What each side knows at each step
pass: Two stations, client and server, with packets that carry readable message names in the order of the standard.
Keys and the certificate appear at a station at the step where that side gets them.
A what-if case: a certificate that fails the check stops the handshake at that step.
Checks cover message order and who holds which key when.
Every protocol claim is sourced to the RFC or a reference that cites it.

evals.prompt: Use the mech skill. Show me how a suspension bridge carries a truck.
pass: Stage 1 is recognisable as a suspension bridge: towers, main cables, hangers, deck, anchorages.
Flow dots show the load path: deck to hangers to main cable to towers and anchorages.
The caption says the bridge is generic and states which sizes are illustrative.
Audit clean.

evals.prompt: Use the mech skill. Show me how a hash table stores and finds a key.
pass: Position has meaning and the caption states it.
One key travels: hashed to a bucket index, placed, then found again by the same path.
A collision case is shown.
Checks cover: the same key always lands in the same bucket.
